title: The one-line tensor contract
allegory: einsum is like a one-line contract at a notary's office: each tensor signs with its axis letters, letters written after the arrow are kept, and letters left off are multiplied together and summed away.
map: the index letters naming each input tensor's axes
the terms written after the arrow, '->bhqk'
a letter both parties sign and the contract keeps
a batch axis: matched entry by entry and carried through
a letter both parties sign but the contract leaves off
a contracted axis: multiplied pairwise, then summed over
one contract instead of a pile of paperwork
one einsum call instead of transpose, matmul and reshape
where_else: Attention scores in one line: einsum('bqhd,bkhd->bhqk', q, k)
Convolution, written as a multiply-and-sum over each window
Reading mech-interp papers, which write weight products and contractions as einsums

hamming.what: A one-line way to multiply and sum tensors by naming every axis with a letter.
hamming.when: Whenever you would otherwise chain transposes, matmuls and sums, most of all for attention scores.
hamming.why: The letters say exactly which axes are matched, kept and summed, so your intent is readable and checkable in one place.
